standard_prerequisites.name: Perfect objects of D(R) and their representation by finite complexes of finite projective modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the representatives on which the formula for c is defined.

standard_prerequisites.name: K_0(R) and additivity of the class map on split short exact sequences of finite projective modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Is the target group and the relation that makes both the surjection step and the telescoping computation work.

standard_prerequisites.name: Distinguished triangles of perfect complexes
standard_prerequisites.use: Fixes the additivity property that the constructed c must satisfy.

core_obligations: Represent a perfect object K by a finite complex M^bullet of finite projective R-modules and define c(K) = sum (-1)^n [M^n] in K_0(R), noting that (1) and (3) will be immediate once this is well defined (proof lines 36508-36517).

For a surjection L^bullet -> M^bullet of finite complexes of finite projective modules with kernel K^bullet, use that each degreewise sequence 0 -> K^n -> L^n -> M^n -> 0 splits because M^n is projective, so that K^bullet is again a finite complex of finite projective modules and c(L^bullet) = c(K^bullet) + c(M^bullet) (proof lines 36519-36529).

For an acyclic finite complex M^bullet of finite projective modules supported in [a, b], break it into the displayed chain of short exact sequences introducing the modules N^i (proof lines 36531-36543).

Argue by descending induction that the N^{b-2}, ..., N^{a+1} are finite projective, that the sequences are split exact, and that the alternating sum telescopes: c(M^bullet) = sum (-1)^n ([N^{n-1}] + [N^n]) = 0 (proof lines 36544-36549).
Conclude formally from the two preceding paragraphs that c is well defined and satisfies additivity on distinguished triangles (proof lines 36551-36557).
difficulty_reason: The lemma asserts the existence of a map c from perfect complexes over R to K_0(R) with three properties: sign behaviour under shifts, additivity on distinguished triangles, and agreement with the alternating sum of classes for a finite complex of finite projective modules (source lines 36490-36505). The proof defines c(K) = sum (-1)^n [M^n] and must show this is independent of the representative (proof lines 36507-36517). It does so in two stages: for a surjection of finite complexes of finite projective modules with kernel K^bullet, the degreewise short exact sequences split because each M^n is projective, giving additivity c(L) = c(K) + c(M) (proof lines 36519-36529); and for an acyclic M^bullet, the complex is broken into the displayed chain of short exact sequences and a descending induction shows each N^i is finite projective, the sequences split, and the alternating sum telescopes to zero (proof lines 36531-36549). Well-definedness and additivity on triangles then follow formally (proof lines 36551-36557). The non-routine step is the telescoping computation for acyclic complexes, which is what makes c well defined.
